name: Jakarta Malay
notes: Glottolog's Betawi. Grijns (1991: 2-5) derives it from a Malay lingua franca of the north Java ports that became a mother tongue and stable dialect in colonial Batavia in the last quarter of the nineteenth century; Adelaar (1994b) takes it as a continuation of Proto-Malayic on the evidence of the final-syllable schwa. Adelaar (2004: 20-23) discusses Nothofer's grouping of Jakarta Malay with Bangka Malay in a 'Southwest Malay' subgroup (decision adelaar1994b-jakarta).
